# Parameter- and classification-recovery study for multilpa().
#
# Data are generated by simulab::simulate_multilpa(), which draws the
# nonparametric two-level mixture of Vermunt (2003): clusters belong to latent
# group classes, a group class fixes profile prevalence inside its clusters,
# and one measurement model is shared by every group. That is exactly the model
# multilpa() estimates, so the generating values are the estimation target.
#
# Truth and estimates are compared by simulab::validate_recovery(). Mixture
# labels are arbitrary, so the estimated profiles and group classes are matched
# to the generating ones before anything is compared; the matching is an
# exhaustive search over permutations, which is exact for the sizes used here.
#
# Run from the project root:
#   Rscript validation/simulab-recovery/recovery-study.R

suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE))
library(simulab)

# simulab 0.4.3 exports the generator as `simulate_ml_lpa()`. This script was
# written against a build that called it `simulate_multilpa()`; the signature is
# unchanged, only the name.
stopifnot(
  "simulab must provide simulate_ml_lpa(); install the sibling simulab >= 0.4.3" =
    exists("simulate_ml_lpa", mode = "function")
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- design ----

indicator_names <- c("reading", "maths", "science", "writing")

true_means <- matrix(
  c(-1.3, -1.1, -1.2, -0.9,
     0.0,  0.3,  0.1,  0.2,
     1.3,  1.1,  1.2,  0.9),
  nrow = 3L, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, indicator_names)
)

# Cluster classes differ only in how common each profile is inside them. Class 1
# is dominated by the low profile, class 2 by the high profile, and the middle
# profile is equally common in both, so the classes are not simply a relabelled
# copy of the profiles.
true_prevalence <- matrix(
  c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10,
    0.10, 0.30, 0.60),
  nrow = 2L, byrow = TRUE
)

true_class_proportions <- c(0.5, 0.5)

conditions <- list(
  list(label = "60 clusters x 20", clusters = 60L, cluster_size = 20L,
       n_starts = 20L, simulation_seed = 10000L, fit_seed = 20000L),
  list(label = "30 clusters x 10", clusters = 30L, cluster_size = 10L,
       n_starts = 20L, simulation_seed = 30000L, fit_seed = 40000L)
)

replications <- 100L
enumeration_replications <- 25L
tolerance <- 0.1

# --------------------------------------------------------------- helpers ----

## All permutations of seq_len(k), one per row.
.permutations <- function(k) {
  stopifnot("`k` must be a single positive whole number" =
              is.numeric(k) && length(k) == 1L && k >= 1 && k == as.integer(k))
  k <- as.integer(k)
  if (k == 1L) return(matrix(1L, 1L, 1L))
  smaller <- .permutations(k - 1L)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(k), function(value) {
    rest <- matrix(setdiff(seq_len(k), value)[smaller], nrow = nrow(smaller))
    cbind(value, rest, deparse.level = 0L)
  }))
}

## Pivot a tidy accessor table back into the matrix the model parameterizes,
## with rows and columns in a stated order rather than whatever order the
## accessor happened to emit.
.as_parameter_matrix <- function(table, value, row, column, columns) {
  wide <- stats::xtabs(stats::reformulate(c(row, column), response = value),
                       data = table)
  result <- matrix(wide[, columns], nrow = nrow(wide),
                   dimnames = list(NULL, columns))
  stopifnot("the accessor must supply one value per cell" = !anyNA(result))
  result
}

.estimated_means <- function(fit, indicators) {
  .as_parameter_matrix(get_results(fit, "profiles"),
                       "mean", "profile", "indicator", indicators)
}

.estimated_sds <- function(fit, indicators) {
  .as_parameter_matrix(get_results(fit, "profiles"),
                       "standard_deviation", "profile", "indicator", indicators)
}

.estimated_prevalence <- function(fit) {
  probabilities <- get_results(fit, "profile_probabilities")
  .as_parameter_matrix(probabilities, "probability", "group_class", "profile",
                       as.character(sort(unique(probabilities$profile))))
}

.estimated_class_proportions <- function(fit) {
  probabilities <- get_results(fit, "profile_probabilities")
  averaged <- aggregate(group_class_probability ~ group_class,
                        data = probabilities, FUN = mean)
  averaged$group_class_probability
}

## The permutation of the estimated labels that sits closest to the generating
## parameters, by summed squared difference.
.best_permutation <- function(estimated, truth) {
  stopifnot("estimated and true parameters must have the same shape" =
              identical(dim(estimated), dim(truth)))
  candidates <- .permutations(nrow(truth))
  cost <- apply(candidates, 1L, function(order) {
    sum((estimated[order, , drop = FALSE] - truth)^2)
  })
  candidates[which.min(cost), ]
}

## Profiles are matched on the measurement model, which is shared by every
## group class; group classes are then matched on profile prevalence, read
## in the profile order just fixed.
.align_fit <- function(fit, indicators, means, prevalence) {
  profile_order <- .best_permutation(.estimated_means(fit, indicators), means)
  aligned <- .estimated_prevalence(fit)[, profile_order, drop = FALSE]
  list(profile_order = profile_order,
       class_order = .best_permutation(aligned, prevalence))
}

.term_table <- function(values, quantity, rows, columns) {
  index <- expand.grid(row = rows, column = columns, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  data.frame(term = sprintf("%s[%s, %s]", quantity, index$row, index$column),
             estimate = as.vector(values), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

.estimates_frame <- function(fit, indicators, alignment) {
  profiles <- alignment$profile_order
  classes <- alignment$class_order
  profile_names <- sprintf("Profile %d", seq_along(profiles))
  class_names <- sprintf("Class %d", seq_along(classes))
  prevalence <- .estimated_prevalence(fit)[classes, profiles, drop = FALSE]
  rbind(
    .term_table(.estimated_means(fit, indicators)[profiles, , drop = FALSE],
                "mean", profile_names, indicators),
    .term_table(.estimated_sds(fit, indicators)[profiles, , drop = FALSE],
                "sd", profile_names, indicators),
    .term_table(prevalence, "probability", class_names, profile_names),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("class proportion[%s]", class_names),
               estimate = .estimated_class_proportions(fit)[classes],
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}

## The truth is read back out of the simulation rather than retyped, so the
## comparison cannot drift away from what was actually generated.
.truth_frame <- function(simulation) {
  parameters <- as.data.frame(simulation, what = "parameters")
  probabilities <- as.data.frame(simulation, what = "profile_probabilities")
  proportions <- aggregate(cluster_class_proportion ~ cluster_class,
                           data = probabilities, FUN = mean)
  rbind(
    data.frame(term = sprintf("mean[%s, %s]", parameters$profile, parameters$variable),
               truth = parameters$mean, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("sd[%s, %s]", parameters$profile, parameters$variable),
               truth = parameters$sd, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("probability[%s, %s]", probabilities$cluster_class,
                              probabilities$profile),
               truth = probabilities$probability, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("class proportion[%s]", proportions$cluster_class),
               truth = proportions$cluster_class_proportion, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}

## `assignments()` is the verb that owns this alignment: one row per input
## individual, in input order, carrying the assigned profile and the group
## class. It replaces reading `what = "posteriors"`, which since the public
## returns were tidied is one row per individual *and profile* -- three times
## as many rows as individuals -- and so silently failed the row-count check.
.classification_accuracy <- function(fit, simulation, alignment) {
  assigned <- get_results(fit, "assignments")
  data <- as.data.frame(simulation)
  clusters <- as.data.frame(simulation, what = "clusters")
  stopifnot(
    "assignments must be one row per input individual, in input order" =
      nrow(assigned) == nrow(data) && identical(assigned$cluster, data$cluster),
    "assignments must cover every generated cluster" =
      setequal(assigned$cluster, clusters$cluster)
  )
  assigned_profile <- sprintf("Profile %d",
                              match(assigned$profile, alignment$profile_order))
  assigned_class <- sprintf("Class %d",
                            match(assigned$group_class, alignment$class_order))
  # One row per cluster for the group-level accuracy: the cluster's class is
  # constant within it, so the first row of each cluster carries it.
  first_of_cluster <- !duplicated(assigned$cluster)
  true_class <- clusters$cluster_class[match(assigned$cluster[first_of_cluster],
                                             clusters$cluster)]
  data.frame(
    individual_accuracy = mean(assigned_profile == data$profile),
    group_accuracy = mean(assigned_class[first_of_cluster] == true_class)
  )
}

.entropy_values <- function(fit) {
  entropy <- get_results(fit, "entropy")
  values <- setNames(entropy$relative_entropy, entropy$level)
  data.frame(individual_entropy = unname(values["individuals"]),
             group_entropy = unname(values["groups"]))
}

.simulate_condition <- function(replication, condition) {
  simulate_ml_lpa(
    clusters = condition$clusters, cluster_size = condition$cluster_size,
    means = true_means, profile_probabilities = true_prevalence,
    cluster_class_proportions = true_class_proportions,
    seed = condition$simulation_seed + replication
  )
}

.replicate_recovery <- function(replication, condition) {
  simulation <- .simulate_condition(replication, condition)
  fit <- multilpa(
    as.data.frame(simulation), vars = indicator_names, id = "cluster",
    n_profiles = nrow(true_means), n_group_classes = nrow(true_prevalence),
    n_starts = condition$n_starts, seed = condition$fit_seed + replication
  )
  alignment <- .align_fit(fit, indicator_names, true_means, true_prevalence)
  recovery <- validate_recovery(
    .estimates_frame(fit, indicator_names, alignment),
    .truth_frame(simulation), tolerance = tolerance
  )
  diagnostics <- data.frame(
    condition = condition$label, replication = replication,
    converged = fit$converged, boundary = fit$boundary,
    best_replicated = fit$n_best_replicated,
    log_likelihood = fit$log_likelihood,
    .entropy_values(fit),
    .classification_accuracy(fit, simulation, alignment),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  if (replication %% 25L == 0L) {
    message(sprintf("  %s: %d replications done", condition$label, replication))
  }
  list(recovery = data.frame(condition = condition$label,
                             replication = replication, recovery,
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
       diagnostics = diagnostics)
}

## Stack one named table out of a list of replication results.
.combine <- function(runs, table) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, function(run) run[[table]]))
}

.run_condition <- function(condition) {
  message(sprintf("Condition %s: %d replications", condition$label, replications))
  runs <- lapply(seq_len(replications), .replicate_recovery, condition = condition)
  list(recovery = .combine(runs, "recovery"),
       diagnostics = .combine(runs, "diagnostics"))
}

## Which (profiles, classes) pair the information criteria select, on the same
## datasets the parameter study used.
.enumerate_replication <- function(replication, condition) {
  simulation <- .simulate_condition(replication, condition)
  candidates <- enumerate_classes(
    as.data.frame(simulation), vars = indicator_names, id = "cluster",
    n_profiles = 2:4, n_group_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 6L,
    seed = condition$fit_seed + replication
  )
  table <- as.data.frame(candidates)
  selected <- function(criterion) {
    best <- table[which.min(table[[criterion]]), , drop = FALSE]
    data.frame(criterion = criterion, n_profiles = best$n_profiles,
               n_group_classes = best$n_group_classes,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  choices <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("aic", "bic_groups", "bic_individual",
                                     "sabic_individual", "caic_individual",
                                     "icl_individual"), selected))
  data.frame(condition = condition$label, replication = replication, choices,
             correct = choices$n_profiles == nrow(true_means) &
               choices$n_group_classes == nrow(true_prevalence),
             all_converged = all(table$converged), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------- summaries ----

.parameter_summary <- function(recovery) {
  averages <- aggregate(cbind(estimate, truth, bias, absolute_error) ~ condition + term,
                        data = recovery, FUN = mean)
  names(averages) <- c("condition", "term", "mean_estimate", "truth", "bias",
                       "mean_absolute_error")
  squared <- aggregate(bias ~ condition + term, data = recovery,
                       FUN = function(value) sqrt(mean(value^2)))
  names(squared) <- c("condition", "term", "rmse")
  rate <- aggregate(recovered ~ condition + term, data = recovery, FUN = mean)
  names(rate) <- c("condition", "term", "within_tolerance")
  merge(merge(averages, squared, by = c("condition", "term")), rate,
        by = c("condition", "term"))
}

.quantity_summary <- function(recovery) {
  recovery$quantity <- sub("\\[.*$", "", recovery$term)
  averages <- aggregate(cbind(bias, absolute_error, recovered) ~ condition + quantity,
                        data = recovery, FUN = mean)
  names(averages) <- c("condition", "quantity", "mean_bias", "mean_absolute_error",
                       "within_tolerance")
  squared <- aggregate(bias ~ condition + quantity, data = recovery,
                       FUN = function(value) sqrt(mean(value^2)))
  names(squared) <- c("condition", "quantity", "rmse")
  merge(averages, squared, by = c("condition", "quantity"))
}

.diagnostics_summary <- function(diagnostics) {
  averages <- aggregate(cbind(converged, boundary, individual_entropy, group_entropy,
                              individual_accuracy, group_accuracy) ~ condition,
                        data = diagnostics, FUN = mean)
  names(averages) <- c("condition", "converged", "boundary", "individual_entropy",
                       "group_entropy", "individual_accuracy", "group_accuracy")
  worst <- aggregate(cbind(individual_accuracy, group_accuracy) ~ condition,
                     data = diagnostics, FUN = min)
  names(worst) <- c("condition", "worst_individual_accuracy", "worst_group_accuracy")
  merge(averages, worst, by = "condition")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- run ----

started <- Sys.time()
runs <- lapply(conditions, .run_condition)
recovery <- .combine(runs, "recovery")
diagnostics <- .combine(runs, "diagnostics")

message(sprintf("Enumeration: %d replications per condition", enumeration_replications))
enumeration <- do.call(rbind, lapply(conditions, function(condition) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(enumeration_replications), .enumerate_replication,
                        condition = condition))
}))
enumeration_summary <- aggregate(correct ~ condition + criterion, data = enumeration,
                                 FUN = mean)
names(enumeration_summary) <- c("condition", "criterion", "selects_true_model")
elapsed <- difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins")

stopifnot(
  "every replication must contribute one row per term" =
    nrow(recovery) == 2L * replications * 32L,
  "no term may go unmatched between estimates and truth" = !anyNA(recovery$bias)
)

cat("\n=== Fit diagnostics, averaged over replications ===\n")
print(.diagnostics_summary(diagnostics), digits = 4)

cat("\n=== Recovery by quantity ===\n")
print(.quantity_summary(recovery), digits = 3)

cat("\n=== Recovery term by term ===\n")
print(.parameter_summary(recovery), digits = 3)

cat("\n=== Structure selected by each information criterion ===\n")
print(enumeration_summary, digits = 3)

cat("\n=== Modal structure chosen, by criterion ===\n")
print(aggregate(replication ~ condition + criterion + n_profiles + n_group_classes,
                data = enumeration, FUN = length))

dir.create("tmp", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(recovery, file.path("tmp", "simulab-recovery-terms.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(diagnostics, file.path("tmp", "simulab-recovery-diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(enumeration, file.path("tmp", "simulab-recovery-enumeration.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(recovery = recovery, diagnostics = diagnostics, enumeration = enumeration,
             means = true_means, prevalence = true_prevalence,
             class_proportions = true_class_proportions, elapsed = elapsed,
             session = sessionInfo()),
        file.path("tmp", "simulab-recovery-study.rds"))

cat(sprintf("\nReplications: %d per condition; enumeration on %d. Elapsed: %.1f minutes.\n",
            replications, enumeration_replications, as.numeric(elapsed)))

.estimates_frame <- function(fit, indicators, alignment) {
  profiles <- alignment$profile_order
  classes <- alignment$class_order
  profile_names <- sprintf("Profile %d", seq_along(profiles))
  class_names <- sprintf("Class %d", seq_along(classes))
  prevalence <- .estimated_prevalence(fit)[classes, profiles, drop = FALSE]
  rbind(
    .term_table(.estimated_means(fit, indicators)[profiles, , drop = FALSE],
                "mean", profile_names, indicators),
    .term_table(.estimated_sds(fit, indicators)[profiles, , drop = FALSE],
                "sd", profile_names, indicators),
    .term_table(prevalence, "probability", class_names, profile_names),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("class proportion[%s]", class_names),
               estimate = .estimated_class_proportions(fit)[classes],
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}

.truth_frame <- function(simulation) {
  parameters <- as.data.frame(simulation, what = "parameters")

  proportions <- aggregate(cluster_class_proportion ~ cluster_class,

  rbind(
    data.frame(term = sprintf("mean[%s, %s]", parameters$profile, parameters$variable),
               truth = parameters$mean, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("sd[%s, %s]", parameters$profile, parameters$variable),
               truth = parameters$sd, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("probability[%s, %s]", probabilities$cluster_class,
                              probabilities$profile),
               truth = probabilities$probability, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(term = sprintf("class proportion[%s]", proportions$cluster_class),
               truth = proportions$cluster_class_proportion, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}

.classification_accuracy.name: .classification_accuracy
documentation: ## `assignments()` is the verb that owns this alignment: one row per input
## individual, in input order, carrying the assigned profile and the group
## class. It replaces reading `what = "posteriors"`, which since the public
## returns were tidied is one row per individual *and profile* -- three times
## as many rows as individuals -- and so silently failed the row-count check.
.classification_accuracy.source:
.classification_accuracy <- function(fit, simulation, alignment) {
  assigned <- get_results(fit, "assignments")
  data <- as.data.frame(simulation)
  clusters <- as.data.frame(simulation, what = "clusters")
  stopifnot(
    "assignments must be one row per input individual, in input order" =
      nrow(assigned) == nrow(data) && identical(assigned$cluster, data$cluster),
    "assignments must cover every generated cluster" =
      setequal(assigned$cluster, clusters$cluster)
  )
  assigned_profile <- sprintf("Profile %d",
                              match(assigned$profile, alignment$profile_order))
  assigned_class <- sprintf("Class %d",
                            match(assigned$group_class, alignment$class_order))
  # One row per cluster for the group-level accuracy: the cluster's class is
  # constant within it, so the first row of each cluster carries it.
  first_of_cluster <- !duplicated(assigned$cluster)
  true_class <- clusters$cluster_class[match(assigned$cluster[first_of_cluster],
                                             clusters$cluster)]
  data.frame(
    individual_accuracy = mean(assigned_profile == data$profile),
    group_accuracy = mean(assigned_class[first_of_cluster] == true_class)
  )
}

.replicate_recovery.source:
.replicate_recovery <- function(replication, condition) {
  simulation <- .simulate_condition(replication, condition)
  fit <- multilpa(
    as.data.frame(simulation), vars = indicator_names, id = "cluster",
    n_profiles = nrow(true_means), n_group_classes = nrow(true_prevalence),
    n_starts = condition$n_starts, seed = condition$fit_seed + replication
  )
  alignment <- .align_fit(fit, indicator_names, true_means, true_prevalence)
  recovery <- validate_recovery(
    .estimates_frame(fit, indicator_names, alignment),
    .truth_frame(simulation), tolerance = tolerance
  )
  diagnostics <- data.frame(
    condition = condition$label, replication = replication,
    converged = fit$converged, boundary = fit$boundary,
    best_replicated = fit$n_best_replicated,
    log_likelihood = fit$log_likelihood,
    .entropy_values(fit),
    .classification_accuracy(fit, simulation, alignment),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  if (replication %% 25L == 0L) {
    message(sprintf("  %s: %d replications done", condition$label, replication))
  }
  list(recovery = data.frame(condition = condition$label,
                             replication = replication, recovery,
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
       diagnostics = diagnostics)
}

.enumerate_replication.source:
.enumerate_replication <- function(replication, condition) {
  simulation <- .simulate_condition(replication, condition)
  candidates <- enumerate_classes(
    as.data.frame(simulation), vars = indicator_names, id = "cluster",
    n_profiles = 2:4, n_group_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 6L,
    seed = condition$fit_seed + replication
  )
  table <- as.data.frame(candidates)
  selected <- function(criterion) {
    best <- table[which.min(table[[criterion]]), , drop = FALSE]
    data.frame(criterion = criterion, n_profiles = best$n_profiles,
               n_group_classes = best$n_group_classes,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  choices <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("aic", "bic_groups", "bic_individual",
                                     "sabic_individual", "caic_individual",
                                     "icl_individual"), selected))
  data.frame(condition = condition$label, replication = replication, choices,
             correct = choices$n_profiles == nrow(true_means) &
               choices$n_group_classes == nrow(true_prevalence),
             all_converged = all(table$converged), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

.parameter_summary.source:
.parameter_summary <- function(recovery) {
  averages <- aggregate(cbind(estimate, truth, bias, absolute_error) ~ condition + term,
                        data = recovery, FUN = mean)
  names(averages) <- c("condition", "term", "mean_estimate", "truth", "bias",
                       "mean_absolute_error")
  squared <- aggregate(bias ~ condition + term, data = recovery,
                       FUN = function(value) sqrt(mean(value^2)))
  names(squared) <- c("condition", "term", "rmse")
  rate <- aggregate(recovered ~ condition + term, data = recovery, FUN = mean)
  names(rate) <- c("condition", "term", "within_tolerance")
  merge(merge(averages, squared, by = c("condition", "term")), rate,
        by = c("condition", "term"))
}

validation/staged-bootstrap-coverage.R.source:
# Interval coverage for a staged fit (`fit_staged()`): the conditional Wald
# errors, which treat the first-stage measurement as known, against the
# two-stage bootstrap (`parameter_inference(method = "bootstrap")`), which
# refits both stages on every resample. Run from the package root:
#   Rscript validation/staged-bootstrap-coverage.R
#
# Data: 80 groups of eight rows in two latent group classes of equal share;
# profile 1 has probability 0.8 in group class 1 and 0.25 in group class 2;
# two Gaussian indicators with profile means (0, 0) and (1.6, 1.4), unit
# variances. The measurement model is correctly specified at the first stage,
# so the staged estimator is consistent and both intervals aim at the same
# values. Profiles are aligned by the first indicator's mean, group classes by
# their probability of profile 1.
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(20260927)
replications <- 150L
bootstrap_iter <- 150L
truth <- c(high_profile_1 = 0.8, low_profile_1 = 0.25, high_share = 0.5)

replicate_once <- function(replication) {
  n_groups <- 80L
  size <- 8L
  n <- n_groups * size
  group_class <- rep(stats::rbinom(n_groups, 1L, 0.5), each = size) + 1L
  profile <- 2L - stats::rbinom(n, 1L, c(0.8, 0.25)[group_class])
  data <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(n_groups), each = size),
                     y1 = stats::rnorm(n, c(0, 1.6)[profile]),
                     y2 = stats::rnorm(n, c(0, 1.4)[profile]))
  quiet <- function(expr) {
    withCallingHandlers(expr,
      latents_unconverged = function(condition) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"),
      latents_bootstrap_dropped = function(condition) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
  }
  fit <- quiet(fit_staged(data, c("y1", "y2"), "g", 2L, 2L, n_starts = 3, seed = 1))
  if (!fit$converged) return(NULL)
  wald <- tryCatch(parameter_inference(fit),
                   latents_boundary_fit = function(condition) NULL,
                   latents_singular_information = function(condition) NULL)
  if (is.null(wald)) return(NULL)
  bootstrap <- quiet(parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap",
                                         iter = bootstrap_iter, n_starts = 2))
  # Profile 1 of the truth has the lower first-indicator mean.
  first <- if (fit$means[1L, 1L] < fit$means[2L, 1L]) "profile_1" else "profile_2"
  profile_rows <- function(table, group_class) {
    table[table$level == "profile" & table$outcome == first &
            table$term == group_class, ]
  }
  group_row <- function(table, group_class) {
    table[table$level == "group" & table$outcome == group_class, ]
  }
  shares <- vapply(c("group_class_1", "group_class_2"), function(group_class) {
    profile_rows(wald, group_class)$estimate
  }, numeric(1))
  high <- names(which.max(shares))
  low <- names(which.min(shares))
  covers <- function(table) {
    rows <- rbind(profile_rows(table, high), profile_rows(table, low),
                  group_row(table, high))
    rows$conf_low <= truth & truth <= rows$conf_high
  }
  standard_errors <- function(table) {
    rbind(profile_rows(table, high), profile_rows(table, low),
          group_row(table, high))$standard_error
  }
  data.frame(replication = replication, parameter = names(truth),
             covered_wald = covers(wald), covered_bootstrap = covers(bootstrap),
             se_wald = standard_errors(wald),
             se_bootstrap = standard_errors(bootstrap),
             estimate = rbind(profile_rows(wald, high), profile_rows(wald, low),
                              group_row(wald, high))$estimate)
}

# One row per parameter: coverage of both intervals and the spread they claim
# against the spread the estimates actually have.
summarise_coverage <- function(results) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(results, results$parameter), function(part) {
    data.frame(parameter = part$parameter[1L], usable = nrow(part),
               empirical_sd = stats::sd(part$estimate),
               mean_se_wald = mean(part$se_wald),
               mean_se_bootstrap = mean(part$se_bootstrap),
               coverage_wald = mean(part$covered_wald),
               coverage_bootstrap = mean(part$covered_bootstrap))
  }))
}

results <- do.call(rbind, parallel::mclapply(
  seq_len(replications), replicate_once, mc.set.seed = TRUE,
  mc.cores = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L)))
summary_table <- summarise_coverage(results)
print(summary_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(summary_table, "validation/staged-bootstrap-coverage.csv",
                 row.names = FALSE)

# Run from the project root: Rscript validation/synthetic-demo.R
# Load the whole package rather than three files by name. The three names this
# script used -- R/fit-ml-lpa.R above all -- stopped existing when the sources
# were reorganised, and sourcing files individually makes a demo depend on the
# internal file layout.
suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE))

set.seed(20260917)
n_groups <- 60L
group_sizes <- rep(c(16L, 20L, 24L), length.out = n_groups)
group_class <- rep(1:2, each = n_groups / 2L)
group_index <- rep(seq_len(n_groups), times = group_sizes)
profile_probability <- c(0.85, 0.15)[group_class[group_index]]
true_profile <- 1L + as.integer(runif(length(group_index)) > profile_probability)
synthetic_data <- data.frame(
  school_id = sprintf("school_%02d", group_index),
  reading = rnorm(length(group_index), c(-2, 2)[true_profile], 0.6),
  maths = rnorm(length(group_index), c(-1.5, 1.5)[true_profile], 0.8)
)
str(synthetic_data)
print(head(synthetic_data))
print(summary(synthetic_data))
print(vapply(synthetic_data, class, character(1)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(synthetic_data), !anyDuplicated(synthetic_data),
          nrow(synthetic_data) == sum(group_sizes))

elapsed <- system.time({
  fit <- multilpa(synthetic_data, c("reading", "maths"), "school_id",
                    n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,
                    n_starts = 8, seed = 42)
})
str(fit, max.level = 1L)
print(dim(fit$subject_posteriors))
print(dim(fit$group_posteriors))
print(head(fit$subject_posteriors))
print(summary(fit))
print(elapsed)

# Align the arbitrary mixture labels before assessing recovery.
profile_order <- order(fit$means[, "reading"])
group_order <- order(fit$profile_probabilities[, profile_order[1L]], decreasing = TRUE)
individual_accuracy <- mean(match(fit$subject_profiles, profile_order) == true_profile)
group_accuracy <- mean(match(fit$group_classes, group_order) == group_class)
stopifnot(fit$converged, !fit$boundary,
          all(is.finite(fit$subject_posteriors)),
          all(is.finite(fit$group_posteriors)),
          max(abs(rowSums(fit$subject_posteriors) - 1)) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(rowSums(fit$group_posteriors) - 1)) < 1e-10,
          all(diff(fit$log_likelihood_history) >= -1e-7),
          individual_accuracy > 0.95, group_accuracy > 0.85)
cat(sprintf("Verified recovery: individual accuracy %.3f; group accuracy %.3f\n",
            individual_accuracy, group_accuracy))
dir.create("tmp", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(data = synthetic_data, true_profile = true_profile,
             true_group_class = group_class, fit = fit, elapsed = elapsed),
        file.path("tmp", "synthetic-demo.rds"))

validation/transition-inference-coverage.source:
# Interval coverage for latent transition models (`parameter_inference()` on
# an `lta()` fit). Run from the package root:
#   Rscript validation/transition-inference-coverage.R
#
# Data: 150 sequences of five occasions, two profiles, one group class; the
# initial distribution is (0.6, 0.4) and the transition matrix has rows
# (0.85, 0.15) and (0.25, 0.75); two Gaussian indicators with profile means
# (0, 0) and (2, 1.6), unit variances. Profiles are aligned to the generating
# labels by the first indicator's mean. Coverage is of the nominal 95% Wald
# interval under the observed information and under the sandwich clustered on
# sequences.
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(20260927)
replications <- 300L
truth <- c(initial_1 = 0.6, stay_1 = 0.85, stay_2 = 0.75, mean_a_1 = 0,
           mean_a_2 = 2, variance_a_1 = 1)
initial <- c(0.6, 0.4)
transition <- matrix(c(0.85, 0.15, 0.25, 0.75), 2L, byrow = TRUE)

replicate_once <- function(replication) {
  frame <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(150L), function(person) {
    path <- Reduce(function(previous, wave) {
      sample.int(2L, 1L, prob = transition[previous, ])
    }, seq_len(4L), init = sample.int(2L, 1L, prob = initial), accumulate = TRUE)
    data.frame(person = person, wave = seq_len(5L), state = path)
  }))
  frame$a <- stats::rnorm(nrow(frame), c(0, 2)[frame$state])
  frame$b <- stats::rnorm(nrow(frame), c(0, 1.6)[frame$state])
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    lta(frame, c("a", "b"), "person", 2L, time = "wave", n_starts = 3,
        seed = 1, tol = 1e-10, max_iter = 5000),
    latents_unconverged = function(condition) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
  if (!fit$converged) return(NULL)
  low <- if (fit$means[1L, "a"] < fit$means[2L, "a"]) 1L else 2L
  high <- 3L - low
  pick <- function(table) {
    row <- function(parameter, outcome, term) {
      table[table$parameter == parameter & table$outcome == outcome &
              table$term == term, ]
    }
    profile <- function(k) sprintf("profile_%d", k)
    rbind(row("initial_probability", profile(low), "group_class_1"),
          row("transition_probability", profile(low),
              sprintf("group_class_1:%s", profile(low))),
          row("transition_probability", profile(high),
              sprintf("group_class_1:%s", profile(high))),
          row("mean", profile(low), "a"), row("mean", profile(high), "a"),
          row("variance", profile(low), "a"))
  }
  observed <- pick(parameter_inference(fit))
  robust <- pick(parameter_inference(fit, vcov_type = "robust"))
  data.frame(replication = replication, parameter = names(truth),
             estimate = observed$estimate,
             se_observed = observed$standard_error,
             se_robust = robust$standard_error,
             covered_observed = observed$conf_low <= truth & truth <= observed$conf_high,
             covered_robust = robust$conf_low <= truth & truth <= robust$conf_high)
}

# One row per parameter.
summarise_coverage <- function(results) {
  table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(results, results$parameter), function(part) {
    data.frame(parameter = part$parameter[1L], usable = nrow(part),
               bias = mean(part$estimate) - truth[[part$parameter[1L]]],
               empirical_sd = stats::sd(part$estimate),
               mean_se_observed = mean(part$se_observed),
               mean_se_robust = mean(part$se_robust),
               coverage_observed = mean(part$covered_observed),
               coverage_robust = mean(part$covered_robust))
  }))
  table[match(names(truth), table$parameter), ]
}

results <- do.call(rbind, parallel::mclapply(
  seq_len(replications), replicate_once, mc.set.seed = TRUE,
  mc.cores = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L)))
summary_table <- summarise_coverage(results)
print(summary_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(summary_table, "validation/transition-inference-coverage.csv",
                 row.names = FALSE)
